summary: Two processes on one SQLite file: no busy_timeout, deferred transactions, and caches that never hear each other
detail: From the v0.5.0 review (TODO #8, Reported). Nothing sets PRAGMA busy_timeout, and writes use db.transaction() (deferred; .immediate() is the fix), so the first write after another process's read lock fails SQLITE_BUSY at once and a valid write 500s. And the in-memory document cache is per process with no invalidation, so two server processes on one file serve divergent state. Either document one process per file as a hard rule (the skill's feature table now says 'one per file') or give SQLite a change channel like the Postgres listener. Repro: two `bun` processes calling registerDocs on the same file, one holding a read transaction while the other writes.
note: 2026-09-24: carried from TODO.md #8; still open after round 2.

summary: A whole-row replace means two things: the JSON file replaces the row, SQLite and Postgres merge the fields sent
detail: From the second review pass (TODO A3). `replace /coll/id` with a partial value drops the missing fields on the JSON-file backend (RFC 6902) and merges them on SQLite and Postgres. The skill's 'Backends side by side' table now says so ('send it whole'). Either registerDoc merges at depth 2 to match, or the SQL backends replace. Repro: scratchpad/delta-reviewer/parity.ts, case 'whole-row replace with partial value'.
note: 2026-09-24: carried from TODO.md A3; documented, not unified.

summary: applyOps is RFC 6901 now but not RFC 6902: add at an array index overwrites, and replace/remove of a missing member do not fail
detail: Round 2 made the pointer grammar strict (leading /, escaping, a segment a string unless its parent is an array, no holes) and batches atomic. Two RFC 6902 rules are still delta's own: `add /arr/1` assigns instead of inserting (pinned by tests/core.test.ts 'add at array index OVERWRITES', documented in core.ts), and `replace`/`remove` of a member that is not there sets it / does nothing instead of failing (so the JSON file acks `remove /messages/nope` where SQLite answers 404). eta keeps its own src/json-patch.ts because it relies on insert (examples/ticker watchlist undo). Making delta's applyOps full RFC 6902 would let eta drop its copy; it changes documented behaviour, so it is Pete's call. Note the client applies broadcasts with the same applyOps, so a strict remove must not break fan-out of a row a client never had.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; for Pete. 2026-09-25 review: lowered to low: documented, pinned behaviour, and a decision rather than a bug.

summary: The server handles a socket's messages concurrently, so a signed-in client that doesn't use onConnect still races its own authenticate
detail: Round 2 fixed the reconnect freeze on the client (connectWs(url, { onConnect }) runs before any doc (re)opens). Without the hook, one thing remains: createWs's message handler is async and not serialised per socket, so an `open` sent right after `authenticate` can be handled first and 401 (the 'variant B' of scratchpad/delta-reviewer/reconnect-auth.ts, re-run as scratchpad/round2-delta-fixer/reconnect-auth.ts). Per-socket serialisation would block slow handlers (recompute, registerMethod), so make it opt-in if it is done.
note: 2026-09-24: the server half of D2; client half fixed in round 2. 2026-09-25 review: the second half (a re-open's 401 only logged, never retried) moved to #17, the same frozen-document symptom; lowered to low, since onConnect is the documented fix for the rest.

summary: SQLite has no auth: no gate, no owns, every socket may open every document of a prefix
detail: D9 from round 1. registerDocs takes no DeltaAuth, and open/delta never ask who is writing, so the SQLite tier cannot be multi-user safe without hand-written ws.on shims. The skill now says 'no auth' in the feature table and the SQLite quick start. A minimal fit with round 2's Postgres design: registerDocs(..., { auth, owns }) with the same default-deny as docTypeFromDef.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; documented, not built. 2026-09-25: history too: SQLite's `history` answers any caller about any document, where the CHANGELOG says 'to whoever may open it'.

summary: SQLite documents have no list mode, and a root row can only be made over the wire by an implied document
detail: D9 / dogfood A3, A4, P5. `defineDoc('todos:', { root: 'todos' })` opened as `todos:` looks for the row id '' and answers 404 (the message now says why). The shape of a document therefore differs from Postgres ({todos} there, {lists, todos} here). implied: true covers creating the root on first write; seeding with SQL covers the rest. Postgres also needs a raw INSERT for a single-mode root row.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; the 404 names the rule now.

summary: SQLite opens and broadcasts carry valid_from and valid_to; Postgres strips them
detail: Seen while writing the SQLite quick start (scratchpad/round2-delta-fixer/sqlite-quickstart.ts): the open snapshot's rows and every echo include the temporal storage columns, which then sit in the client's doc.data. Postgres runs _delta_strip_temporal on both. inverseOf already strips them (withoutStorage). Stripping them on SQLite too would make the document shape the same on both SQL backends.
note: 2026-09-24: found in round 2; not fixed.

summary: Two validateOps: SQLite's (types, root fields) and Postgres's (a subset, which the listener never calls)
detail: CLAUDE.md used to say validateOps lived in src/schema.ts, shared; it does not. sqlite.ts has the full one; postgres/schema.ts exports a smaller one for callers, and the Postgres listener relies on delta_apply's checks instead (round 2 added unknown and required fields there). One shared validator is the DRY answer, but Postgres list-mode documents address rows on the root collection where SQLite treats /<root>/<x> as a root field, so it needs the document's mode.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal.

summary: doc.data is typed as a writable Signal, so an optimistic doc.data.set() type-checks
detail: Round 1 (delta.md §4). The skill's first rule is 'never optimistically update', but Doc<T>.data is ReturnType<typeof signal<T|null>>, so .set() and .patch() compile. Exposing ReadonlySignal<T|null> would make the rule a type error. It is a type-level breaking change for anyone who calls set() today.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal.

summary: The CLI is not agent-safe yet: no in-band token, watch never exits, only ops that land on a ledger come back
detail: Round 1 (delta.md §4, §5). An auth-enabled server can't be reached (the token must not go in the URL, so it needs an in-band `call authenticate` first: --token / DELTA_TOKEN); `watch` never exits, so a Bash tool call hangs (--count N, --for 5s); `delta` returns only {ack}, not the ops as applied (--print-ops); and there is no offline `validate` or server `describe`. These come before an MCP wrapper.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal. 2026-09-25 review: `delta` now prints the whole answer (ops, inverse, version, entry on a ledger backend); still missing: a token, a watch that exits, and offline validate / describe.

summary: CI installs the latest Bun unpinned
detail: ci.yml has `bun-version: latest` and publish.yml no version, so a Bun release can turn the gate red with no change here (round 1 saw exactly that on 1.4.2; the teardown was fixed upstream in 0.6.0).
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal; release tooling is Pete's. 2026-09-25 review: the Docker-gate half moved to the shared /publish item, kept in eta.

summary: A memory document's add /coll/- stores the key "-"; the JSON file and SQLite mint an id
detail: Round 2 made `add /<coll>/-` on a collection of rows mint an id on the JSON file (server.ts mintIds) and SQLite. registerMemory applies ops with applyOps directly, so `/people/-` on an object makes the key '-'. Memory documents are written by the server, so it bites less; mintIds could move to core for both.
note: 2026-09-24: found in round 2; not fixed.

summary: The test surface is not shared: mockClient and sendAndAwait are not in the package, and the pointer vectors are one test file's, not data eta can run
detail: Consumers can't import mockClient/sendAndAwait (tests/ is not in the package; the skill now says so). And the one pointer grammar is pinned by VECTORS in tests/postgres-pointer.test.ts, run through splitPath and _delta_split_path; as a JSON fixture (wire-vectors.json) eta's json-pointer.ts could run the same cases without a dependency (proposal-final.md §4). The team's larger idea is backend conformance stories (who does what, who sees it) run against JSON, SQLite and Postgres; tests/create-row.test.ts and tests/error-codes.test.ts are the first two. The walk planners too (was #21): planWalk and _delta_walk_plan are one rule in two languages with no shared cases; a list of { entry: { ops, inverse }, current, expected: { ops, conflict } } run through both would pin them as the pointer vectors pin the two parsers. And eta's side of the wire law (was eta #22): the same vectors, as data, run by eta.
note: 2026-09-24: round-2 proposal. 2026-09-25 review: #21 merged here.

summary: On a temporal table, an explicit id the sequence later mints, or two adds of one id at once, make two live rows
detail: The 409 on an add of a live id (5bbff72) is an EXISTS check before the INSERT, and a temporal table's key is (id, valid_from), so nothing in the database stops a second live version. (1) `add /tnotes/1` then `add /tnotes/-`: nextval mints 1, the `-` branch skips the check, and the table holds two live rows with id 1 while `open` shows one (the first is lost). (2) Two adds of one explicit id through two documents (different doc locks) both pass the EXISTS check. Repro: scratchpad/round2-delta-reviewer-2/pg-temporal-id.test.ts (DELTA_TEST_PG_URL at a scratch database). Candidates: a partial unique index `(id) WHERE valid_to IS NULL` from codegen (a migration for existing tables), or setval past an explicit id, or refuse explicit ids other than undo's re-add.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; not fixed (needs a schema change).

summary: A subscription outlives the right to hear it: owns is asked at open, a token's exp at the next request
detail: With auth, `owns` is asked when a socket opens a document and on each request, and jwtAuth's gate checks `exp` on each request; nothing checks either between requests. A socket taken off a document (owns now false) or whose token ran out keeps receiving every write through what it has open until it next asks for something. And when that request comes, jwtAuth drops the socket's subscriptions but leaves it connected, so the client's documents freeze with `connected` true and onConnect never runs again (the skill now says to re-authenticate and re-open on the 401). Repro: scratchpad/round2-delta-reviewer-2/pg-revoke.test.ts: Alice opens `items:`, is taken out of `owns`, Bob writes, and Alice's socket receives the add. Options: a `revoke(identity, docName)` / `dropIdentity` hook the app calls, owns re-asked per subscriber in drainDoc (a query per write per subscriber), and for expiry closing the socket (e.g. code 4401) so the reconnect runs onConnect with a fresh token. Also (from #5): a document whose re-open got a 401 is only logged, never retried after a later authenticate (client.ts).
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; design question.

summary: An onConnect that calls through DI (call("authenticate", params) with no client) deadlocks: the client never connects, and says nothing
detail: onConnect runs before `ready` resolves, and only the client it is given skips `ready`. `connectWs(url, { onConnect: () => call("authenticate", { token }) })` with `provide(WS, ...)` sends through inject(WS), which waits for `ready`, which waits for onConnect: `connected` stays false for good, no document opens, and nothing is logged. The docs show the right form (`(ws) => call(..., ws)`), but it is one missing argument. Repro: scratchpad/round2-delta-reviewer-2/onconnect-di.ts (HANG, connected: false). Options: a log.warn when onConnect has not settled after a few seconds, or a request made from inside onConnect's async context going straight out.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; not fixed.

summary: SQLite applies a batch's field writes after its adds and removes, so a batch that changes a row and then removes it is a 404
detail: applyOps in sqlite.ts collects field replaces (and whole-row replaces) into rowFieldBatches and writes them after the loop over adds and removes. `[replace /items/y/name, remove /items/y]` fails 'Row not found: items/y' (the JSON file and Postgres apply it in order), and a batch's ops are not applied in the order sent. Found writing the net-change walk test (222f3ae): the SQLite case uses remove-then-add instead. Either apply in order, or say in the skill's side-by-side table that a SQLite batch writes fields last.
note: 2026-09-24: found by the round-2 review; low.

summary: No law per document: nothing proves a copy equals a fresh read from the tables after every change
detail: epsilon's proveLaw drove a document type's ops over the real wire and checked, after every echo, that the client's copy deep-equals a fresh composition from the tables, undo and mirrors included, naming the likely defect when not. delta has no such harness, so a fan-out, cascade or echo that diverges from the tables is found by an app, if at all. A `proveLaw(doc, drive)` for both backends, over a socket, with undo and every document holding the rows checked.
note: 2026-09-25: from the survey of every completeness check from dzql to eta. 2026-09-25 review: lowered to low: a test harness, not something a user hits.

file: src/sql/001d-delta-write.sql (delta_apply), src/sql/001b-delta-scope.sql (_delta_row_in_scope), tests/postgres-fanout.test.ts, tests/postgres-isolation.test.ts, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/delta-doc/, tests/helpers/fanout.ts, tests/sqlite-fanout.test.ts
summary: Postgres is wrong: a write is told only to the document written through. Both backends must fan out the same way, and on Postgres the fan-out belongs in the database, in delta_apply
detail: THE GAP (read in the code, 2026-09-25). SQLite forwards a write to every other open document that holds the row (sqlite.ts fanOut + rowInScope, after the commit). On Postgres, delta_apply ends with _delta_bump_and_notify(p_doc_name, ops): one document's next version, its ops in _delta_ops_log, one NOTIFY with its name. The listener (listener.ts onNotification -> drainDoc) fetches that document's ops and publishes them on that channel only, plus customFanOut for custom documents. So a board and a household over the same rows, or a venue's map and a promoter's occasion over the same sites, disagree until one is reopened. CLAUDE.md calls the difference an invariant ('Fan-out differs by backend, on purpose'); it is wrong, and tests/postgres-fanout.test.ts and tests/postgres-isolation.test.ts pin it. THE PLAN (not built; for review). On Postgres a document is a definition in _delta_docs that the stored functions interpret, so the database, not Bun, works out who else holds a changed row. (1) In delta_apply, for each changed row and every _delta_docs definition whose root or include has the row's collection (other than the written document), find the document names that hold it: a single-mode definition by walking the row's parent chain to that definition's root (the walk _delta_row_in_scope already makes), giving prefix || root_id; a list-mode definition, or an unparented collection (every document of the prefix holds it), by the names of that prefix in _delta_versions that _delta_row_in_scope accepts. Only names in _delta_versions count: a document never opened is not told. (2) Rewrite the ops per target as sqlite.ts fanOut does: the target's root row becomes replace /<coll> (null on remove); a source root-level replace /<coll> becomes /<coll>/<id> where the target holds <coll> as a map; otherwise the op as it is. (3) Collect per target and call _delta_bump_and_notify once per target per write, so each target gets one version and one NOTIFY per write, in the writer's transaction. For a remove, find the targets before the row is deleted or closed, including the rows _delta_cascade_remove takes with it. CONSEQUENCES: the Bun listener is unchanged (every process relays each document's NOTIFY to its own subscribers); undo, redo and delta_apply_as get it too (checked: delta_apply_as, delta_apply_logged and the walk at 001g line 255 all go through delta_apply); every told document gets its own version, so catch-up after a reconnect works and a client that misses one sees the gap. TESTS: turn postgres-fanout.test.ts round (the household hears the board's write as its root; the menu hears a course and its drink); move the fan-out cases into a property run on both backends, as tests/helpers/isolation.ts is; the isolation suites must still pass on both. DOCS: CLAUDE.md's invariant becomes 'fan-out is the same on both backends'; delta-doc SKILL.md (line 198) and reference.md's Fan-out section; CHANGELOG: the framework SQL changes, idempotently (CREATE OR REPLACE), and consumers re-vendor it (bunx @blueshed/delta init). Then eta: its reference says a change arrives 'whether this process wrote it or another did over Postgres', which is not yet true for defined documents.
note: 2026-09-25: from the survey of every completeness check from dzql to eta. 2026-09-25, later: reopened as wrong, not a design choice (Peter). OPEN QUESTIONS, not yet checked, to settle in review before building: (a) dzql's subscribables and seiro modelled this before: read how they found the documents a row write touches, and take what they learned. (b) _delta_versions is never pruned (checked: nothing deletes from it), so it holds every name ever opened, not the ones open now: is telling long-closed documents acceptable, or does the listener need to say which names are open? (c) Cost: list-mode and unparented targets mean a scan of _delta_versions by prefix and a _delta_row_in_scope per name; the index on doc_name and a range test on the prefix need checking at allertons' scale (261 venues, 14.7k sites, 1,350 occasions). (d) RLS: the fan-out runs as the writer (app.user_id). A parent row the writer cannot see would hide a target the owner can see; should the membership walk be SECURITY DEFINER? (e) Custom DocTypes registered from TypeScript (registerDocType, not in _delta_docs) are outside the database's view: are they told, and how? (f) NOTIFY order and de-duplication inside one transaction: confirm in the Postgres documentation, not from memory. (g) SQLite tells only open documents and without a version (#29); should SQLite gain versions so the two are the same on the wire too? TESTS (written before any fix, 2026-09-25): tests/helpers/fanout.ts holds one schema, one seed and 22 cases asked of both backends (tests/sqlite-fanout.test.ts, tests/postgres-fanout.test.ts), each ending on the law of #27: every open copy, with what it was told applied, equals a fresh open. tests/postgres-fanout.test.ts adds a second process on the same database, a told document's version and catch-up from delta_fetch_ops, no version for a document never opened, list-mode documents, and keeps the writer's-channel tests it replaced. Now: SQLite passes 19 of 20 shared cases; Postgres fails every case in which another document must be told (23), each because nothing was told, and passes the four that say who must not be. FOUND BY THE TESTS: (h) Moving a row by writing its parent key: SQLite refuses it ('Unknown field: weddings_id'), Postgres accepts it (_delta_assert_fields lets the parent key through). Decide: moves allowed and told on both, or refused on both. The two move cases fail on SQLite until decided. (i) The plan finds the documents a row is in after the write; a complete fan-out also tells the documents it left: a list-mode document whose condition it no longer meets, and a single-mode one whose root it no longer hangs from, must hear a remove, and the writer's own document too when the row leaves it. The plan must find the targets before the write as well as after. (j) A temporal row: SQLite shows valid_from and valid_to in opens and broadcasts (checked by running it), Postgres strips both (_delta_strip_temporal). Not fan-out, but the backends differ; the shared cases compare rows without them.

summary: Fan-out publishes carry no version, so a client cannot notice one it missed
detail: A write's own publish carries `v` (with a ledger) and the client resyncs on a gap; the publishes fan-out sends to other documents carry none, so a missed one is undetectable and the copy stays wrong until re-opened.

summary: A custom document watching a root collection is never told of a write to a root row
detail: customFanOut matches rows by collection, and a write to a document's root row is published as a root-level op that the custom document's membership never sees (probe, 25 Sep, around sqlite.ts:806); it stays stale until re-opened.

summary: An included grandchild whose parent collection is not included loads differently on the two backends
detail: Found while fixing #2. `_delta_load_collection` walks up to a parent the document does not include and loads its children anyway: `user:` with include ["memberships"], memberships under teams (no parent), loads every team's memberships on Postgres (teams in full) and none on SQLite (loadCollection returns [] for an ancestor with no parent that is not included, which is what rowInScope and tests/write-scope.test.ts 'cascadeOn is not scope' expect). A parented ancestor that is not included (root -> a -> b, include ["b"]) is walked on both, but SQLite's rowInScope needs the parent in the document's cache, so such a b row is loaded and never fanned out. Needs a decision: refuse an include whose parent chain leaves the document (at registerDocs / generateSql, where the schema is known), or walk it the same everywhere.
note: 2026-09-25: found fixing #2; not changed (the Postgres side is the framework SQL contract).
